title: Possible dwarf planets: New discovery could rewrite what we know about the solar system

content:
The solar system could soon have a sixth officially recognized dwarf planet. Astronomers have detected a mysterious object beyond Pluto, provisionally named ED138, although its classification has yet to be confirmed.

If further observations validate its status, ED138 would join Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake, and Eris, the five dwarf planets currently recognized by the International Astronomical Union (IAU).

An Unexpected Discovery Among Billions of Observations

The discovery originated at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile, a facility that began operating in 2025 at an elevation of 8,800 feet (2,682 meters). It houses the world's largest digital camera, capable of photographing the entire visible sky every three days.

Matthew Holman, a Smithsonian astrophysicist and Harvard astronomy lecturer, identified ED138 while using software he helped develop to analyze billions of astronomical detections collected in 2026.

The finding caught him so off guard that his first instinct was to check the system for possible errors. He described his initial reaction as one of “excited disbelief.”
